body:
Corrected by probe in round 5; the earlier reading was wrong.

A session is gone when its shell exits: `zmx run x -d exit` and the name vanishes from `zmx ls` and the socket disappears, at once. So 'ended sessions are just gone' is true of attach-style use.

`ended=<epoch>` and `exit_code=<n>` are task-scoped, not session-scoped: they appear when a command dispatched with `zmx run` finishes, and the session stays alive and reusable (a later `zmx run` on the same name reuses it and clears the field). Verified by dispatching `true` into a session, waiting 16s, then running another command in the same session.

Consequence: `ended` must never be read as 'dead'. A reader that skips ended records — as dl-zmx.el does — silently drops live, attachable sessions whose last task finished. The elisp comment 'Exited sessions stay listed with an ended field' is wrong on both halves.

Still true and useful: `zmx ls` prints name, pid, clients, created, cwd, then every label; one parse yields identity, activity and model.
title: zmx lifecycle: session death and task end are different things
